radiology_report:
Maastricht UMC+ Radiology Division | 10 February 2025 | Modality: Multiparametric MRI of the Prostate

Clinical context: 63-year-old male with ascending PSA curve (current 5.5 ng/mL) and a history of a positive previous biopsy. Reassessment of the existing PI-RADS 4 lesion.

FINDINGS:
The gland occupies 48.0 mL. Asymmetry characterizes the peripheral zone. A discrete focus sits in the posterior right mid-gland peripheral zone, spanning 14 × 10 × 12 mm. T2 sequences highlight pronounced hypointensity within this region. Corresponding diffusion restriction manifests as low ADC values. Early focal enhancement stands out against adjacent tissue on dynamic contrast sequences. Seminal vesicles appear normal. Pelvic lymph nodes show no suspicious enlargement, and capsular extension is absent.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 4 lesion in the right mid-gland peripheral zone.
PSA density: 0.11 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.6454933.

previous_notes.author: Dr. K. Bakker (GP)
previous_notes.text: Clinic visit today noted a PSA value of 4.5 ng/mL recorded in May 2024, continuing a steady climb first documented in late 2023. Taking into account the prior positive biopsy results alongside this consistent marker elevation, the clinical picture has been updated. The gentleman denies any current urinary dysfunction, though he notes ongoing lower back stiffness that continues to require physiotherapy.
